root_cause.text: Missing bounds check on the size of the flexible array `Buffer` in `struct smb2_query_info_rsp` against the actual received response buffer length (`rsp_iov[1].iov_len`) before copying `qi.input_buffer_length` bytes to userspace, allowing a malicious server to specify an `OutputBufferLength` larger than the response data and cause an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `struct_size(qi_rsp, Buffer, qi.input_buffer_length) > rsp_iov[1].iov_len` to prevent copying beyond the response buffer. The CVE description notes that the QUERY_INFO branch "never verifies that the flexible-array payload actually fits within rsp_iov[1].iov_len" and that a malicious server can "return OutputBufferLength larger than the actual QUERY_INFO response, causing copy_to_user() to walk past the response buffer".

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds check to avoid out-of-bounds read in SMB2 query info response handling.
intent_record.what: Added a guard that if qi.input_buffer_length > 0 and the total size of qi_rsp (including its variable-length Buffer) exceeds rsp_iov[1].iov_len, set rc = -EFAULT and jump to out label.
intent_record.how: After adjusting qi.input_buffer_length based on the server's OutputBufferLength, the patch validates that the response structure fits within the received iov. If it does not, it returns an error, preventing potential out-of-bounds access when subsequently copying data to user space.

candidates.rationale: This conditional adjusts input_buffer_length based on OutputBufferLength but does not check that OutputBufferLength is within the bounds of the actual response buffer (rsp_iov[1].iov_len). A malicious server can set a large OutputBufferLength, causing an out-of-bounds read when data is later copied using the adjusted input_buffer_length.

This assignment sets input_buffer_length to the server-controlled OutputBufferLength without validating it against the actual buffer size. This value is subsequently used for copying data to userspace, leading to an out-of-bounds read.

Combined with the subsequent assignment, a malicious server can set a large OutputBufferLength that exceeds the buffer, leading to an out-of-bounds read.
